phase_A.phase: A: corrected empirical event-response kernel estimation
phase_A.event_age_convention: response age 0 is the first aligned IV response; response age -1 is the Notebook 15 driver row
phase_A.notebook15_lag_relationship: Notebook 15 lag +1 equals response age 0; lag +2 equals response age +1
phase_A.continuous_support_rule: start at earliest relevant event index minus abs(min response age) plus selected AR order
phase_A.other_bank_rule: include all other-bank events whose response-age interval overlaps continuous support
phase_A.complementary_same_bank_rule: include nuisance response-age controls for excluded target-bank events in contamination and early-late sensitivity models
phase_A.ar_order_rule: reuse a unique Notebook 15 order or select background-only BIC order 1 through 10
phase_A.parametric_decay_definition: descriptive signed A exp(-lambda tau), unrestricted amplitude and non-negative decay rate
major_limitations: Weights are empirical statistical response coefficients, not known data-generating weights or structural causal effects.
Daily IV fixing time is unknown and alignment remains material.
The signed exponential is descriptive and does not replace the nonparametric kernel.
phase_A.forecasting_status: Forecasting has intentionally not yet been implemented; Phase B will use training-window-estimated weights only.

phase_B.forecast_target: daily USDJPY 1M ATM IV change and implied next IV level
phase_B.AR_order_selection_rule: background-only BIC inside each training window
phase_B.calendar_information_assumption: final historical scheduled calendar treated as ex-ante; no revision, cancellation, or unscheduled-decision model
phase_B.DM_specification: two-sided HAC DM-style mean loss differential, maxlags=min(10,n-1)
phase_B.BH_correction_families: within alignment, evaluation subset, and loss function across two event models
major_limitations: Final historical calendar is treated as ex-ante schedule.
One-step expanding-window evidence is predictive rather than causal.
Phase A exponential summaries were weak or unusable descriptive fits.
phase_B.full_sample_phase_A_weights_statement: Full-sample Phase A weights were not used as forecast coefficients. All event weights were re-estimated inside each chronological training window.
phase_B.common_BIC_sample_rule: At every origin, the maximum-lag training matrix is filtered once and every p=1,...,10 candidate uses those identical outcome dates.
phase_B.condition_number_validation: Every fitted background and event-aware design is required to be full rank with a finite condition number.
phase_B.sign_aware_predictive_loss_classificatio: BH-significant positive background-minus-event loss differentials are improvements; negative differentials are underperformance.

phase_C.interval_construction_method: Asymmetric empirical training-residual quantiles using lower and higher quantile methods.
phase_C.training_only_residual_rule: Predictive intervals were calculated from empirical quantiles of residuals available within each training window. Future forecast errors and full-sample residuals were not used.
phase_C.interval_comparison_method: Two-sided HAC mean difference of background minus event interval scores, maxlags=min(10,n-1).
phase_C.BH_correction_families: within alignment, evaluation subset, and nominal coverage across two event models
major_limitations: Residual-quantile intervals are empirical rather than exact Gaussian or structural confidence intervals.
The final historical calendar is treated as an ex-ante schedule.
Forecast comparisons are predictive and do not establish causality.
